commits.message:
Document the l1_index_unconfigured readiness reason

The node refuses to start when its L1 index cannot be built from the
deployment and configuration; operators need the reason's text and its
public presentation entry like every other readiness reason.

Read deployment status from the deployment's own outputs, never by address

Deployment status read every protocol component by scanning its script
address, which on a local node is a full ledger scan and timed out on
preprod. It is now one exact-output read: the hub-oracle nonce plus the
recorded initialization transaction's outputs. Initialization creates
every component at once and the hub-oracle output can never be spent,
so that output alone shows the deployment landed; the partial state is
gone.

init records each attempt, with its validity bound, before submitting.
An attempt whose bound has passed while the nonce is unspent can never
land, so status reports empty and init builds again instead of waiting
forever. Status needs no contracts while the nonce is unspent, so the
harness checks the nonce right after creating it. The readiness probe
finds the hub-oracle output among the initialization outputs and keeps
that reference. init on a complete deployment reports the real
initialization hash.

Open the node's L1 reader with its full index, so it never scans

The node's reader started with an empty tracked set and adopted the
follower's recorded set later; until then any protocol read fell back to
a full ledger scan. One definition of the node's index (protocol set,
own wallets, projections) now serves the follower and the reader, so
both record the same set and the reader tracks it from the open. A read
before the follower's first cursor is follower:not_initialized.

Chain parameters (the slot mapping) are a keyed ledger query and no
longer go through the reader, which removes the cycle between the
reader and the contracts it is configured from.

Read the cancelled orphan's state from one /proc read

PID 1 may reap the killed grandchild between an existence check and a
second read of its stat file, which failed the test with ENOENT. The
process identity already carries the state from a single read.

Build a resumed stack's images again so new code reaches its containers

A resumed run confirmed running services from one readiness snapshot
whenever their generated configuration was unchanged. Nothing in that
configuration names the source the node, committee and watcher images
are built from, so a run resumed after new commits kept testing the
containers an earlier run had built.

Each harness run now carries a build id. A services record confirms
only when this run built it; a record from an earlier run starts the
services again, which builds the images (cached when nothing changed)
and lets Compose recreate only the containers whose image changed. An
attached public node still confirms by its pinned release image.

Let the watcher dial the loopback DA peer its config admits

The config parser admits a local-only stack's own 127.* DA peers on a
named network (stackLoopbackPeers), but the libp2p transport only
dialed ip4 peers on a Custom chain. A preprod twin's watcher therefore
parsed its retained-DA peer and then refused to dial it, so it could
never fetch a block's DA payload.

The transport now has one rule: it dials an ip4 peer only when the
admitted config, re-parsed, lists that exact peer and the verified
identity's network and protocol match. Which ip4 peers a config may
hold stays the parser's decision alone. The runtime always passes its
admitted config.

The harness's public-DA check now reports each failed attempt instead
of only the header hash.

Generate MDX types after Next loads the docs configuration

Next typegen loads the Fumadocs configuration and starts its asynchronous generator. Await the explicit MDX generator afterward so TypeScript reads a completed generated module. This ordering fixes the documentation check exposed while verifying the module refactor.
Keep historical source evidence linked to its original commit
Point the transaction source map at the new module owners

Read the stack's wallets through Kupo, not the local node's ledger

The live harness checked wallet funding, the operator's hub-oracle nonce
and the user's deposit funds with the node's l1-utxos over its default
access: an address query against the local node's ledger, which scans
the whole UTxO set and does not fit a command's deadline on preprod.
The twin run stopped at the wallet check with node_timeout.

These reads now go through the stack's Kupo and Ogmios, the same view
the user's own midgard-user already reads through.

Give HTTP, Phase B and test fixtures clear module owners

Group declarations by domain responsibility instead of extraction order.
HTTP separates routes, public reads, operator actions, readiness and submission
resources. Phase B separates UTxO overlays, candidate graphs, input resolution
and script execution. Shared fixtures separate transaction material, proof
construction, scenario ownership and explicit test resources.

Carry the latest branch behavior into these owners, including its removal of
the deposit-build endpoint and deposit-submission records. Retain the public
surfaces and module limits, including the existing 717-line retirement ceiling.
Move only the affected lint-baseline and size-exception paths. Point the HTTP
source guard at the complete implementation directory.

Pure moves against 7b37c1730b88 confirmed 316 declaration groups on 2026-11-03:
HTTP 99, Phase B 51, submit-init fixtures 67, database fixtures 47 and collection
fixtures 52; all five verifier commands exited 0. Import targets, evaluation
order, compiled boundaries and behavior require their separate review/checks.

Extend source guards to inspect module directories

Allow an explicit implementation directory to include nested source modules,
so source guards continue inspecting code when cohesive modules replace
same-prefix file facets. Existing file/facet discovery remains unchanged.

The nested-directory regression fails against the previous helper at its
path-list assertion. node --test scripts/lib/source-facets.test.mjs passed
4 tests, 0 failed, exit 0 on 2026-11-03.

Document deposits and withdrawals with midgard-user

The node guides, the docs site and the acceptance reference now send users to
midgard-user, with its provider requirement: a Kupo that indexes the wallet
and the deposit or withdrawal list (or everything) and keeps spent outputs, or
Blockfrost.

Drop the node's user submission tables

Migration 0031 drops event_history_submission_inputs,
event_history_submissions and deposit_submission_attempts, children first and
without CASCADE, so an unexpected dependent fails the migration instead of
being dropped silently. The registry moves to schema version 31.

Delete the node's user deposit and withdrawal submission path

Deposits and withdrawals are built, recorded and confirmed by the user's own
midgard-user tool, so the node no longer carries any of it: the
submit-deposit, reconcile-deposit-submission and submit-withdrawal commands,
the durable history-submission driver with its history-nonce lock, input
reservations and takeover, the submission and attempt database modules, and
the SDK's checkpointed submission state machine. Their tests go with them;
behavior that still matters is covered by the SDK and midgard-user tests.

The node keeps its own intent journal for its own transactions, genesis
deposits and the L2 transfer command. The read-only L1 comparison view no
longer fills deposits' admission-hash column from an Order's location, so the
column has one meaning: the admission transaction the follower recorded.
